_note: Glossary words whose Jastrow entry cites this pasuk for this word but with a different reading (girsa) or spelling of the Targum. Shown as a note in the pop-up. Oct 23.
pagla: Jastrow files this pasuk under פְּגַר III (פִּגְרַיָּא), the reading of ed. Bon. Ed. Berliner and others read פַּלְגַּיָּא, and a manuscript has פִּגְלַיָּא, close to our text’s פַּגְלַיָּא.
qamohi: Jastrow cites this pasuk with a different reading, ומִדְּקַדְּמוֹהִי. Our text has וּמִדְּקַמּוֹהִי, close to ed. Berliner’s מִדְּקָמוֹהִי.
shivkha: Jastrow’s entry follows a manuscript reading, שִׁבְּבִין. The printed editions, like our text, have שִׁבְכִין.
immatai: Jastrow has this word spelled לְאֵימַת. Our text has לְאִמָּתַי.
qartsul: Jastrow spells this word with ס, קַרְסוּלִּין. Our text has קַרְצוּלִין.
saarta: Jastrow spells this word with ס, סְעַרְתָּא. Our text has שׂ.
ruvta: Jastrow reads כְּרוּבַת as one word, כְּרוֹבָא (a measure of land). The glossary takes it as כְּ + רוּבַת.
hidda: Jastrow cites this pasuk with a different reading, חוֹדְיָן (ed. Berliner), and notes חִידְוָן in ed. Amsterdam. Our text has חִדְוָן.
karqom: Jastrow’s main reading here is with כ, כַּרְכּוֹמִין. Our text has ק, כַּרְקוֹמִין, a spelling he also lists.
ribbona: Jastrow’s form is רִבּוֹנְתָּא; our reading here, רִבָּנְתִּי, is the one he gives for ed. Vienna.
